segs.text: SKUdesk. One agent that finds the cheapest price, works out what a resale would keep, and checks for arbitrage. Only on the exact same product.

Here's the problem. A cheap listing is only a deal if it's the same item. Price sites mix up an iPhone 16 and a 16 Pro, or a phone and its case. We check that first, and a person approves every purchase.

Let's try a Apple iPhone 14, 128 gigabytes. The agent searches Google Shopping right now. Gemini reads every listing and decides if it's the same phone. Watch the graph: each result lights it up. Green is the same phone, red is a different one.

Then Gemini looks at each photo, and our code checks that the words it quoted are really in the listing. Here's the answer: the cheapest identical price, the cost of reselling it, and every listing we turned down, with the reason. These are asking prices from Google Shopping.
Not every check ends in a deal. For the Pixel 9 Pro, nothing could be proven identical, so the agent says no. We think an honest no is more useful than a wrong yes.

The market page shows what the agent knows. Sellers' prices sit on the book, with the gap. Below them, four buyer strategies bid what they could pay after costs. A deal needs a bid that reaches the best price. You can also turn the product around in 3D.
Every product we watch is in this list, each with its own book and its own price history. A scheduler checks them for us, around the clock.
When the agent does find a buy, it files a proposal. Only the person who ran the check, or the owner, can approve it. The agent never spends money by itself.
After approval, the owner can list the resale in Google Merchant Center. It's previewed first, and this is a real, connected account.
How do we know the gate works? We labelled sixty-seven pairs of listings by hand: phones, LEGO, clones, bundles, even listings with hidden instructions. It made no wrong match, and missed none.
SKUdesk runs on Google Cloud: Cloud Run, Firestore, Scheduler, Secret Manager, Gemini and the Merchant API. It's live at skudesk dot lol. Thanks for watching.
